content:
ankur: hey folks, onboarding day 3. tried to build runtime from source and hit a weird error during JIT/PTX compile for sm_80:

ankur: build command:
```
cmake -B out -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ..
cmake --build out -j8
```

ankur: error snippet:
```
ptxas fatal   : Unresolved extern function '_Z9foo_kernelv' referenced from .o section
nvlink error : unresolved symbol: _Z9foo_kernelv
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

ankur: nvcc is 11.8 on this image but the base image in our dockerfile uses CUDA 12.1. I suspect mixed toolkits again. who do I bother about aligning the toolchain?

jules: welcome @ankur! that ptxas/nvlink unresolved extern usually means kernel name mangling mismatch or that object compiled for different PTX target. first check `nvcc --ptxas-options=-v` and ensure `-gencode` arch flags are consistent across compile units. Also confirm `CUDA_HOME` and `/usr/local/cuda` point to the same toolkit.

lina: +1. run `grep -R "-gencode" third_party | sort -u` to see if a vendored lib forces a different SM target. We had a similar hit when a prebuilt third_party blob was compiled for sm_75 and our host used sm_80. Rebuilding that blob fixed it.

ankur: quick outputs:
```
$ echo $CUDA_HOME
/usr/local/cuda-11.8
$ ls -l /usr/local/cuda
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 15 Apr 10 09:00 /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1
```

ankur: so headers are from 12.1 but CUDA_HOME points to 11.8. messy.

jules: choose one toolkit. Easiest: update CUDA_HOME to /usr/local/cuda (which now points to 12.1) and clean build: `rm -rf out && cmake -B out -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda ..`. If you must keep 11.8, change symlink instead.

ankur: switched CUDA_HOME to /usr/local/cuda and rebuilt. got past nvlink but now failing tests with ABI symbol mismatch: `undefined symbol: _ZNSt6vectorIiE6resizeEm` from a prebuilt lib in third_party.

lina: that is libstdc++ ABI mismatch. are you on an older distro? `g++ --version`? Our recommended dev image uses GCC 11. If you can't upgrade system g++, use the docker dev image `redwood/dev-runtime:toolchain-ubuntu20` like the README suggests.

build-bot: note: CI images use ubuntu20 + gcc-11; building locally on older distros may require toolchain container. See https://intranet.redwood/dev-images#toolchains

ankur: I'm on Ubuntu 18 (old laptop). I'll switch to the dev container and re-run. thanks for the quick triage.

jules: quick tip: when you open your onboarding PR, include a small note in docs saying "If your host distro<20 use the toolchain dev image". We get this question a lot.

ankur: will do. thanks! pairing welcome later if anyone's free. :smile:
